children: , the AI-memory and storage powerhouse, entered Monday's scheduled mediation with labor tensions at its critical Taiwan manufacturing base still unresolved. Shares gained approximately 2.4% to $1,039.67, extending a powerful run fueled by tight memory supply and booming AI demand. The valuation picture shows just how aggressively investors are pricing that momentum: Micron trades 61.79% above its $642.61 GF Value estimate.

The dispute centers on money. Two unions representing more than 80% of Micron's roughly 15,000 Taiwan employees are pushing for a permanent system allocating 15% of global operating profit to workers. No strike had been called when Reuters reported on the negotiations September 15, while Micron said it would participate in mediation in good faith. That distinction matters. Investors are not dealing with an actual production shutdown yet, but the possibility of disruption at Micron's largest manufacturing base puts labor negotiations directly alongside supply and pricing as variables worth watching.

And Micron has plenty of profit to fight over. Its latest quarter delivered an 84.6% gross margin and $33.32 billion of operating income, numbers that show how extraordinary the current memory cycle has become. A one-time bonus rewards employees when conditions are exceptional; permanent profit sharing would structurally raise labor costs whenever earnings surge again. That creates a delicate equation for shareholders: keeping Taiwan operations stable is enormously valuable, but so is preserving as much of AI-driven memory scarcity's margin windfall as possible.

title: Micron Gains 2.4% as Taiwan Labor Talks Reach Decision Day
